title: Terraform module for private EKS control plane provisioning with canary health orchestration (Orbit)
creator: Asha Khatri
description: Build a reusable Terraform module ("Orbit") to provision Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs. The module must encapsulate the control plane bootstrap, networking preflight checks, KMS key wiring, IAM roles, and a built-in canary health orchestration hood that validates cluster control-plane readiness and automates safe rollbacks for provisioning-related failures. This is intended to replace ad-hoc scripts and hardcoded patterns across on-prem/VPC deployments and to be consumable by the Private control plane provisioning pipeline.
background_and_motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require deterministic, auditable provisioning of EKS control planes across multiple accounts and VPC topologies. Current provisioning is brittle: manual preflight steps, inconsistent KMS wiring, and limited automated health checks cause long lead times and operational toil. Orbit is meant to centralize safety checks, reduce incidents during upgrades, and provide clear observability hooks for the Console and SRE runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes documented inputs/outputs for VPC IDs, private subnets, KMS key ARN, control-plane tags, and bootstrap IAM role
Preflight step validates: route table attachments, NAT gateway presence (if required), DNS delegation for private zone, and KMS key grants before starting control plane create
Canary health orchestration runs 3 validation phases (API availability, node registration, control-plane latency) and reports PASS/FAIL to a defined S3/CloudWatch metric
On canary failure the module triggers a controlled rollback sequence that removes partial resources and leaves a remediation artifact (terraform state tag + CloudWatch event)
Module supports an opt-in 'immutable-canary' boolean to enable creation of a temporary canary cluster that can be destroyed automatically when validations pass
Comprehensive unit/integration tests run in CI (terraform validate + terratest or equivalent) and a smoke test in a dedicated sandbox account
Documentation with examples for: standard VPC, shared-services VPC with cross-account KMS, and an air-gapped/on-prem wiring pattern
No plaintext secrets in state; KMS keys and IAM role ARNs are referenced and ownership boundaries documented
technical_notes: Module will be implemented as a set of smaller modules: networking-preflight, eks-controlplane, iam-bootstrap, kms-wiring, canary-orchestration
Use EKS managed control plane (eksctl/terraform-aws-eks) patterns but ensure ability to swap to an internal operator in later release via a 'control_plane_provider' variable
Canary orchestration will be driven by a Lambda step function: coordinate health probes, emit metrics to CloudWatch, and write artifacts to a versioned S3 path
State locking: enforce remote state with DynamoDB lock and strict state pathing per-account/cluster to avoid collisions
Terraform provider versions pinned; CI will run 'terraform plan' with TFC/remote runner and fail on drift in plan automation
Potential future extension: integrate with Redwood Console rollout APIs to surface canary progress and remediation recommendations
tasks: Design module input/output schema and write examples (done: initial draft)
Implement networking-preflight checks with explicit failures for missing route53/KMS grants
Implement eks-controlplane resources with tags and control-plane role wiring
Add kms-wiring helper to create/grant keys or validate cross-account key ARNs
Build canary-orchestration (lambda + stepfunction) and unit tests for probes
Add CI jobs: terraform validate, fmt, plan; terratest sandbox run for smoke test
Write docs + upgrade playbook for existing clusters to migrate to Orbit
Security review and KMS/IAM policy audit
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Architecture reviewed with SRE and Security. Agreed on step-function approach for orchestration and KMS cross-account patterns.
2026-03-04: Prototype of networking-preflight implemented; early checks for route table and private hosted zone pass in sandbox account.
2026-03-08: eks-controlplane module scaffolding completed. IAM bootstrap role policy drafted; awaiting least-privilege review from Security.
2026-03-10: Canary-orchestration Lambda skeleton pushed (PR #1789). Integration tests for probe sequence in progress. Assigned remediation artifact format for console ingestion.
test_plan: Unit-level: terraform validate and static checks on HCL
Integration: terratest create/destroy in sandbox with mocked KMS cross-account grants
Canary: create temporary cluster with immutable-canary=true and assert probes within 15 minutes
Failure injection: simulate missing KMS grant and ensure preflight fails and does not begin control plane creation
Upgrade path: run migration example on an existing sandbox cluster and validate no downtime for caller endpoints
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental exposure of secrets in state. Mitigation: require SSE-KMS for state S3 bucket and deny plaintext variables in CI. Add a linter check.
Risk: cross-account KMS grants are complex and brittle. Mitigation: provide a 'validate_kms_grant' step that can run as a dry-run and explicit error messages
Risk: automated rollback could leave orphaned resources. Mitigation: rollback sequence includes tagging and a cleanup lambda that runs with escalation alerts in case manual cleanup is required
Risk: provisioning time variability could cause CI flakes. Mitigation: increase probe timeouts and run canary in a longer-running sandbox account with retries
